doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Ali's drumming influences and stretching phrases
summary: Ali on Philly Joe Jones, Roach, Blakey and Elvin, and developing his stretched-out style alongside Cecil Taylor and Sunny Murray.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So most of your people that you listened to, you saw them in New York, you’re — it’s sort of people that you wanted to emulate or heard on records? Is that right?

Yeah. I mean like a lot of the players that I listened to like Philly Joe Jones was my first love and Max Roach and Art Blakey and Elvin Jones, you know that changed my way of playing because I heard in Philly Joe Jones the way he stretched out phrases. You know, and he would just do it for a little while, like he would stretch the phrase out and just for maybe two or three bars, then he would go back to the swing. And I was wondering, I’d say wow, I wonder what would happen if he just kept stretching it out? Just keep stretching it out a little bit before you go back to the swing but keep in mind where the time is and where everything else is, but just keep, just keep — and then I listened to Art Blakey and Max Roach and I felt like they all, actually they all were avant garde drummers to me, because they were all playing the beat but they were just like doing little things inside the beat that I really listened to. So I’ve worked on that. I worked on that. And I tried to just stretch it out and elongate it until I was sort of playing that way all throughout everything else. But at the same time keeping time and keeping tempo and keeping changes running through my head but just elongating it, just letting it all just stretch out. And I think that’s how I sort of developed my style of playing. And then listening to people like Cecil Taylor and — Henry played with all these people — I listened to people like Cecil and Henry Grimes and all those guys who were stretching out that stuff, right, and Sunny Murray, another drummer who was doing that, and Milford Graves, Andrew Cyrille, it was all kinds of just trying to play something different, you know, and it all came together actually. So that’s how I felt about it.
